name: @atusy/tsudoi-workspace
//devDependencies: THE FRAMEWORK IS DECLARED HERE AND NOT ONE FIELD UP, RULED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED, and the field is load-bearing twice over. It is what makes examples/tsudoi.config.ts and the consumer-shaped fixtures resolve tsudoi BY NAME with no `paths` mapping left anywhere. And `devDependencies` is deliberately not a build edge (scripts/workspaces.ts), so this declaration does NOT order the framework before the root -- this root carries no build config after the move, so the builder skips it and its position decides no artifact. The derived order is asserted byte for byte in test/build-order.test.ts, which is where a slip into `dependencies` would show up rather than in a test written for it. WHAT IT COSTS, WRITTEN DOWN SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED: this entry hands every member a SECOND route to the framework through the root's node_modules, and it silently disarmed two controls a probe had stated in advance -- so every control perturbing a MEMBER'S OWN route must stash this one too. The three upstream packages are here because the ROOT PROGRAM imports them directly, by bare specifier, in its own test files; an undeclared import that happens to resolve through a member's install is the fragility this repository keeps closing. AND `yaml` IS HERE FOR A REASON THE OTHERS ARE NOT, MEASURED: bun placed it in the MEMBER that declares it rather than hoisting, and this repository's staging arms (test/unbuilt-checkout.test.ts, test/own-subpaths.test.ts) build a stage whose node_modules is borrowed ENTRY BY ENTRY FROM THIS ROOT -- so a member's own runtime dependency that exists only under packages/ makes every staged build fail on TS2307 for it, which is a red about the apparatus. The root program does not import it.
//name: A NAME THAT APPEARS IN NO REGISTRY, NO CONSUMER'S MANIFEST AND NO EXECUTED COMMAND BLOCK, and it is distinct from the framework's on purpose. Two packages claiming one name is `one package spelled two ways` in the one place the member guard cannot see -- that guard iterates members and this is not one -- and MEASURED on bun 1.3.13 the failure mode is SILENCE: bun refuses two MEMBERS by name and by line, and accepts a ROOT and a member sharing a name with no warning at all, a third package's specifier then resolving to the member with nothing saying so. Dropping `name` is refused for the SAME reason rather than a different one: a nameless root is missed silently too. It must not be a prefix-extension of the published name, which a recorded boundary exists to refuse.
//private: PERMANENT, AND IT IS NOT THE PUBLISH SENTINEL. This root ships nothing and never will, so the key here can never become the edit that permits publication -- which is exactly why test/optional-peer-premise.test.ts LOCATES the framework's manifest by the name it declares instead of reading this file. A premise keyed here would answer `publication is forbidden` by construction, for ever, measuring nothing.
